title: p-adic Hodge parameters in locally analytic representations of GL_n
summary: Construct the quotient-deformation comparison for generic noncritical crystabelline (φ,Γ)-modules and use its kernel to select a minimal locally analytic representation of GL_n(K). The plan proves parabolic and embedding compatibility, recovery of modified Hodge flags, scalar character statements, and the first-order Artinian universal-extension reformulation. Its two input theories are imported with explicit unresolved supplier contracts.
readme:
The classical smooth representation together with the Hodge–Tate weights fixes a locally algebraic representation, but in rank at least three it leaves Hodge flags undetermined. This roadmap records how Ding’s comparison detects those extra parameters inside extensions of locally analytic representations. Its first output is a canonical surjection t_D:B→Q. The kernel selects π_min(D), whose embeddingwise pieces recover precisely the modified objects D_σ. A second description realizes the same representation as the maximal-ideal annihilator of a universal extension with an Artinian action.

This is a local comparison roadmap. It imports the entire GL_n representation theory from LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (design #3411) and the entire trianguline/Hodge theory from TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel (design #3412). Neither supplier has a roadmap definition, reserved stage or packet in this checkout. The reader specifies their exact contracts and records gaps; provisional requests to existing foundational stages are filing references, not evidence that those stages already provide the missing theories. The design pass is complete, but no layer is closed and no theorem is implemented. In rank two the kernel is zero and π_min=π_1, so this construction adds no Hodge parameter. It is expected to be far smaller than the full locally analytic representation of a p-adic correspondence. Ding’s global applications in §4 belong to the separate local-global compatibility roadmap.

The six layers follow mathematical dependencies: common refinement parameters; comparison and kernel; minimal extensions and scalar characters; parabolic and embedding compatibility; recovery; universal Artinian actions. The definitive targets, APIs, discriminating tests, source corrections and ownership boundaries are in research/blueprint/readmes/PadicHodgeParametersInLocallyAnalyticRepresentations.md. Every source statement is restated in our own words, with locators in the published 74-page version.

stages.title: Refinement parameters and the common presentation
stages.description: Define endpoint refinement families and determinant-pullback block character directions; prove their telescoping spanning formula. Form the two surjective maps from the sum of quotient trianguline tangents to representation Ext and quotient deformation space. This layer imports all underlying representation and deformation objects.

stages.title: Ding’s comparison and its kernel
stages.description: Glue the two endpoint block comparisons under rank induction, prove compatibility with every refinement using block-character spanning, and obtain the unique surjection t_D. Compute its kernel dimension c_n d_K and its transversality to every trianguline direction.

stages.title: The minimal extension and its scalar characters
stages.description: Construct the tautological kernel extension π_min and its finite-slope pushout; identify its Ext group with Q, characterize it by socle layers and refinement maps, and prove the determinant-normalized group-center and infinitesimal-character scalar actions.

stages.title: Parabolic and embedding compatibility
stages.description: Compare parabolic block kernels and their maximal push-forward subextensions. Construct the σ comparison and maximal partial algebraic minimal representation, split the kernel by embeddings and amalgamate over A. Transport comparison to D_σ without imposing regularity at the modified embeddings.

stages.title: Recovery of modified Hodge parameters
stages.description: Extract from the two parabolic minimal subextensions the embedded higher-intertwining relation in its fixed block ambient space. Prove π_min(D)_σ≃π_min(D′)_σ exactly when D_σ≃D′_σ, and deduce the full family and K=Q_p consequences.

stages.title: Universal extensions and first-order Artinian actions
stages.description: Form A_D and A_{D,w} as first-order algebra fiber products, equip the universal refinement extensions with their parameter-ring actions, and construct the unique A_D-action on the full universal extension. Identify its maximal-ideal annihilator with π_min(D).
